IREN.summary: At the All-In Summit in Los Angeles, Kent Draper, Chief Commercial Officer of IREN, joined NYSE Live to discuss the rapid evolution of AI infrastructure, growing demand for compute resources, and the next phase of artificial intelligence adoption. Draper explains how IREN operates as a vertically integrated AI cloud company, providing compute services through company-owned data center infrastructure. He discusses how controlling the underlying physical assets enables the company to support customers across a range of AI workloads while expanding capacity to meet growing demand. A significant portion of the conversation focuses on the challenges associated with scaling AI infrastructure. Draper highlights the importance of land, power, labor, supply chains, and execution as the industry works to increase available compute capacity. He explains why bringing new capacity online remains one of the most important challenges facing AI infrastructure providers. The interview also explores the company's long-term outlook for artificial intelligence. Draper discusses his view that AI computing differs from traditional cloud computing and examines how the growing need for AI-specific infrastructure is creating new opportunities across the technology sector. Another major topic is financing. Draper shares insights into the development of financing markets designed to support AI infrastructure projects and discusses the increasing availability of capital for compute and data center expansion. He explains how customer commitments and financing structures are evolving alongside industry growth. The discussion further examines the durability of AI demand and the emergence of real-world use cases. Draper points to applications in manufacturing, research and development, drug discovery, enterprise operations, and customer-facing technologies as examples of how AI adoption continues to expand across industries. Toward the end of the interview, Draper highlights the concept of physical AI, including robotics and AI-enabled manufacturing technologies. He discusses why these areas are attracting increased attention and how advances in artificial intelligence may increasingly influence the physical economy. Throughout the conversation, Draper provides perspective on AI infrastructure, cloud computing, data center development, capacity planning, financing trends, enterprise adoption, and emerging applications of artificial intelligence.
